raw_response:
Well, let me think through this year like I always do...

I'm getting on now, 65 years old, and with just me and my daughter-in-law at home most days — my son's off in the city — I can't work like I used to. I've been on these 15 mu for forty years though, so I know the ground.

I'll put garlic on about 2 mu near the house, where the soil is good and the well is close. Garlic brings in cash but it's a lot of work — planting cloves one by one, pulling the scapes in May, digging the bulbs. I get the village women to help for a few days and pay them or trade. Every year I keep back some bulbs from harvest for next year's seed, but I'll still need to buy a bit more good seed.

The other 13 mu goes to wheat now through June, then maize right after, like everyone around here does. If you don't double-crop you're just leaving money in the dirt.

For fertilizer, I do what my husband always did — two bags of compound fertilizer per mu when we plow for wheat, then one bag of urea per mu when it turns green and starts jointing. If the wheat looks yellow I put a little more, if it's dark I hold back. Maize gets one bag of compound before seeding and a scoop of urea when it's knee-high. Garlic I feed more generously, plus sheep manure from my neighbor who keeps a small flock.

Water costs money now since they put the meter on the well. Wheat I give three waterings — green-up, jointing, grain-fill — skip one if the spring rains come. Maize only if it really doesn't rain, usually twice. Garlic takes more, four or five times through the season.

Spray — wheat once before heading for the aphids and rust. Maize I don't spray unless I see armyworm. Garlic I spray two or three times for the rot, otherwise you lose the whole field and all that work is wasted.

Nephew plows cheap with his small tractor. I hire the cooperative's big machine for wheat planting and combining. Everything in the garlic field is by hand. Last year wheat gave me 850 jin per mu, maize 1100 jin, garlic 2000 jin. Should be about the same this year if the weather holds.
